From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Sarah Bennett <sarah@launchco.com>, Alan Cho <alan@launchco.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 09:45:30 -0800
Subject: Re: Launch traffic: 429 errors spiking during ramp

Team — initial SRE triage below (top-line):
- Observation: 09:05–09:13 PST: 429 rate for LaunchCo rose from baseline 0.7% to peak ~18%. Concurrent small spike in 503s from a small fraction of model backend VMs that hit memory pressure and timed out.
- Cause hypothesis: Combined effect of a planned aggressive client ramp without client-side exponential backoff + our per-tenant concurrency limiter (default conservative setting) triggering early throttles. The concurrency limiter then caused backlog and queue timeouts on a couple of older model-serving nodes; retries from clients amplified the load (retry storm).

Immediate mitigations executed (09:38 PST):
1) Temporarily increased per-tenant concurrency cap for LaunchCo by 3x (in-bound routing rule) — reduced 429s by ~55% in preliminary telemetry.
2) Shifted a subset of ramp traffic to a warm fallback model variant with lower memory footprint to reduce tail latency.
3) Enabled accelerated autoscaling policy for LaunchCo pool (lower CPU/latency thresholds).
4) Applied transient request queuing backpressure to smooth peaks (short window).

Request to LaunchCo: please reduce aggressive client retries (advise exponential backoff with jitter). We can provide recommended retry config for your SDK.

Follow-up items:
- Post-incident: Review default concurrency limiter profile for planned launches; consider launch-specific ramp profiles in Redwood Console.
- Engineering: debug why a small subset of model-serving VMs hit memory pressure under the same model variant (possible kernel-level allocator regression).

Attachment: runbook-429-mitigation.pdf (playbook steps).

Looping in execs for visibility. Summary for leadership: LaunchCo experienced a planned traffic spike for LaunchDay that interacted poorly with their client retry policy and our conservative per-tenant concurrency limiting. SRE has applied temporary mitigations and is actively bringing 429s down.

Proposed leadership actions:
- Approve a one-time LaunchDay ramp policy template: temporary 3x concurrency cap + accelerated autoscale + warm fallback model routing for the first 30 minutes of planned product launches.
- Consider offering LaunchCo a credits package for the impact window (to be discussed with Finance).

I'm marking this as P1 and request quick sign-off on the ramp template so we can proactively enable it for subsequent launches. Neha — please include a short changelog and rollback criteria.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
